primary_category.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: I pulled the case file to set up my analysis parameters... I built out the allele table, flagged the ambiguous loci, and moved into the comparison stage.
evidence.explanation: The core task is gathering case documentation, generating and reviewing electropherogram data, and evaluating allele-level evidence to determine contributor status.

evidence.quote: I spent a good amount of time on those — peak heights, confirming they weren't stutter, checking the ratios.
evidence.explanation: Evaluating peaks for authenticity and matching against a reference profile is direct evidence-evaluation work.

evidence.quote: We only had the homeowner's elimination sample at that point. I flagged internally that the ex-boyfriend and delivery driver were unsampled.
evidence.explanation: Identifying gaps in the evidentiary record and assessing which sources require further verification is evaluative information work.

evidence.quote: Quantity came back under 100 picograms on quant, so I knew going in this was going to be a low-template situation — lots of stochastic effects, peak height imbalance.
evidence.explanation: Interpreting a quantitative measurement (picogram quantity) to infer downstream analytical implications is a numeracy task.

evidence.quote: The likelihood ratio came back moderate, not overwhelming.
evidence.explanation: Generating and interpreting a likelihood ratio is an explicit statistical/numerical reasoning task central to forensic DNA reporting.

evidence.quote: with low-template DNA, you do get dropout and occasional artifact peaks, so logging them as inconclusive isn't unusual practice.
evidence.explanation: Applying a general model of low-template DNA behavior (stochastic effects, dropout, artifacts) to interpret specific case data is abstraction/diagnostic reasoning beyond simple data lookup.

evidence.quote: When I wrote the narrative section, I pulled those together with the DNA finding into one account.
evidence.explanation: Composing a written report narrative synthesizing findings is a literacy-based communication task.

evidence.quote: my supervisor was the only technical reviewer available that week, so whatever I produced, she'd be the one signing off, fast.
evidence.explanation: The analyst must coordinate report completion timing with a single available technical reviewer and the DA's hearing deadline, reflecting dependency management, though this is a constraint description rather than the analyst actively coordinating others.

A1.2 Dexterity - no description of manual lab manipulation (e.g., pipetting, swabbing) in the interview text

A2.1 Uncodified visual/auditory processing - electropherogram interpretation involves some pattern recognition but the interview frames it primarily as rule-based comparison against thresholds and known profiles, better captured under A2.4/A2.5
A2.6 Creativity, planning and resolution - the analyst follows standard intake and comparison procedures; no evidence of generating a novel solution or multi-step contingency plan
A3.1 Serving and attending - no direct interaction with victim or suspect described as service provision
A3.2 Teaching, training, coaching - not present

A3.3 Selling and influencing - the analyst states a preference for a coherent narrative for the DA, but this is a reporting/drafting choice, not an act of persuasion or negotiation observed in the interview
ambiguities: A2.1 vs A2.4: electropherogram peak interpretation could be framed as uncodified perceptual pattern recognition (A2.1) or as evidence evaluation (A2.4). The interview describes it primarily through evaluative language ('spent time on', 'dug into', 'checking ratios') rather than perceptual signal detection, so A2.4/A2.5 were favored, but A2.1 is a defensible alternative with lower confidence.

A3.3 vs A2.2: the choice to write a unified narrative for the DA's office has a persuasive flavor, but the interview frames it as a drafting/reporting decision rather than an interpersonal influence attempt, so it was excluded from secondary categories rather than included as A3.3.

evidence.quote: I didn't request rush swabs from either of them... I treated that as an open question for someone else to chase, not something that needed to hold up the report.
evidence.explanation: The analyst exercises discretion over whether to pursue further testing and how to frame the report, but operates within externally set deadlines and submission procedures, indicating moderate rather than high latitude.

evidence.quote: my supervisor was the only technical reviewer available that week, so whatever I produced, she'd be the one signing off... My supervisor reviewed it quickly given her own deadline and signed off.
evidence.explanation: Work is subject to mandatory technical review and sign-off, but the review in this episode was described as quick and did not substantively probe open items, indicating real but limited monitoring intensity.

evidence.quote: I finished the report and sent it up for technical review the night before the hearing.
evidence.explanation: The analyst depends on a detective's submission information, a victim's follow-up call, and a supervisor's review, showing coordination with multiple parties, though most of the analytic work itself is performed individually.

evidence.quote: I pulled the case file to set up my analysis parameters — stochastic threshold, amplification target, all standard.
evidence.explanation: Setting standard analysis parameters is described as routine intake practice repeated across cases.

evidence.quote: Honestly, it's just how intake works. You read the submission form, you see what the detective knows, you set your parameters.
evidence.explanation: The analyst describes a fixed intake and analysis procedure (quant, amplification, stochastic threshold, allele table) applied consistently.

evidence.quote: Quantity came back under 100 picograms on quant, so I knew going in this was going to be a low-template situation — lots of stochastic effects, peak height imbalance.
evidence.explanation: The analyst anticipates and encounters unpredictable stochastic effects, dropout, and unexplained peaks, indicating low certainty in the evidentiary inputs.

evidence.quote: A few days later the victim called back and mentioned an ex-boyfriend had been in the house three days before the break-in, and a delivery driver had been at the door earlier that week. That complicated the elimination picture.
evidence.explanation: The analyst must respond to new, unexpected information disrupting the elimination framework mid-case, requiring an adaptive but still deadline-bound response.

tools.role_in_task: Generating and analyzing electropherogram data, allele tables, and likelihood ratio calculations for DNA mixture interpretation

evidence.quote: Then I ran the amplification... I built out the allele table, flagged the ambiguous loci, and moved into the comparison stage.
evidence.explanation: Amplification, electropherogram generation, and allele-table construction rely on specialized forensic DNA-analysis software and instrumentation beyond ordinary office tools, though the interview does not name specific systems.

evidence.quote: The likelihood ratio came back moderate, not overwhelming.
evidence.explanation: Likelihood ratio computation for mixture interpretation is typically produced via specialized probabilistic genotyping or DNA-analysis software.

tools.role_in_task: Reading case submission forms and drafting the written report

evidence.quote: I finished the report and sent it up for technical review the night before the hearing.
evidence.explanation: Producing and transmitting a written case report implies use of standard document and communication software, though this is not explicitly described.

task_anchors.task_description: Receiving a rush DNA case submission with detective notes and setting standard analysis parameters based on quant results
Reading detective's narrative and suspect information before examining the electropherogram
Interpreting electropherogram peaks, building the allele table, and documenting matching versus missing/unexplained alleles
Weighing suspect-inclusion evidence against unsampled alternative contributors named by the victim
Synthesizing the likelihood ratio with non-genetic case facts into a final written report for technical review
